lessonRef.subject: mathematics
lessonRef.unitTitle: Complex Solutions, Polynomials, and the Binomial Theorem
lessonRef.focus: closure and arithmetic of rational expressions
lessonRef.title: Performance task build: closure and arithmetic of rational expressions

sections.title: Guided practice
sections.directions: Set up the first two carefully; the rest of the build depends on them.

items.prompt: In the expansion of (x + y)^4, find the coefficient of the term x^1·y^3.
Complete the statement: the quotient of two rational expressions, where the divisor is not the zero expression …
choices: is always a rational expression, because dividing is multiplying by the reciprocal
is always a rational expression, because a common denominator can always be formed
need not be a rational expression, because the denominators may differ
is always a rational expression, because numerators and denominators multiply directly

sections.title: Independent practice
sections.directions: Work on your own. Show the steps that produced each answer.

items.prompt: Factor x² + 36 completely over the complex numbers.
choices: (x + 6i)²

items.prompt: A polynomial with real coefficients has degree 6. How many roots does it have in the complex numbers, counted with multiplicity, and what constrains its non-real roots?
choices: exactly 6, and any non-real roots occur in conjugate pairs
exactly 7, and any non-real roots occur in conjugate pairs
exactly 3, and any non-real roots occur in conjugate pairs
exactly 5, and any non-real roots occur in conjugate pairs

items.prompt: In the expansion of (x + y)^6, find the coefficient of the term x^2·y^4.
Complete the statement: the product of two rational expressions …
choices: is always a rational expression, because dividing is multiplying by the reciprocal
is always a rational expression, because a common denominator can always be formed
need not be a rational expression, because the denominators may differ
is always a rational expression, because numerators and denominators multiply directly

items.prompt: Factor x² + 9 completely over the complex numbers.
choices: (x + 3i)²

items.prompt: A polynomial with real coefficients has degree 3. How many roots does it have in the complex numbers, counted with multiplicity, and what constrains its non-real roots?
choices: exactly 2, and any non-real roots occur in conjugate pairs
exactly 3, and any non-real roots occur in conjugate pairs
exactly 4, and any non-real roots occur in conjugate pairs
exactly 6, and any non-real roots occur in conjugate pairs

sections.title: Extension and challenge
sections.directions: Carry the build to a result and state the check that would catch an error in it.

items.prompt: In the expansion of (x + y)^7, find the coefficient of the term x^5·y^2.
items.responseExpectation: Give the result and the reasoning that produced it. Show enough work that someone else could check each step.
